$Comment: The base every zc encounter script builds on. It is Abstract, so it never spawns on its own: a
boss is a Variant of it (Type Variant, Reference Zc_Encounter_Base, Modify the parameters below)
or a Generic script that copies its shape.
What it does, in order. A Player sensor with the EncounterMembers collector keeps the roster the
boss bar and the music are applied through, and the roster the library credits presence from. In
Intro, while nothing is bound in SubjectSlot and the site has rested, TriggerSpawners fires the
SpawnMarker within SummonRange and binds the first spawn into the slot; the moment the Target sensor sees it, the
boss is made vulnerable, any crowd-control rule a phase left on it comes off (ZigControlRule, so a boss that got
away mid-fight starts the next one on its own rules), the bar goes up under BossBarName, the Music starts, the arena's volumes
tagged ArenaTag hear Engaged, the zc:engaged beat tells the library the fight is on, and the state
moves to Fight. In Fight, the FightBehavior slot runs whatever macro a Variant hands it (Zc_Adds_Wave,
say, or a macro of your own on the Hytale.Instruction.Encounter.Phase.Behavior interface), and the
moment the Target sensor loses the boss the defeat beat clears the bar, stops the music, clears any sky a
phase set (SetEncounterWeather), releases the slot, tells the arena's volumes Defeated and sends zc:defeated. Complete first pays
DefeatReward, a ZigClaim reward under Server/Rewards, to every player the win credited (left empty, it pays nothing),
then waits RearmSeconds, sends zc:reset and returns to Intro, so the same entity runs the fight again the next time
a player comes near.
Who wakes it and who is in it. The boss rises for a player within SensorRange; with WakeInArena true that
player must also wear WakeMark, which an ArenaWake volume (tools/rooms) puts on whoever stands inside the arena,
so a player outside the door never starts the fight. Members, the bar and the music reach every player within
ArenaRange (SensorRange when smaller), and the empty-arena reset waits until no living player stands within it,
so set ArenaRange to cover the arena's far corners and ledges.
Phases. A fight with more than one hands Phase2Transition a transition macro (Zc_Phase_At_Health,
its numbers through _ForwardedModifiers), which moves the fight to Phase_2 and runs Phase2Behavior
there; Phase3Transition and Phase3Behavior go on to Phase_3 the same way. EveryPhase runs beside each
phase's own behaviour in all three, for what the whole fight does (a timer, health packs, a hint).
A transition may also change which crowd control lands on the boss from then on (Zc_Phase_At_Health's
SetControl and Control), and a behaviour may open a short window with the game's own ApplyEntityEffect
(UseTarget) naming a timed rule effect such as Zig_Control_Stun_Window.
Every slot left $Null does nothing, so a one-phase fight writes none of them. Each phase keeps the
same defeat check.
The arena reset (ArenaReset true): a wipe (every player in the arena's range down) or an arena left with no
living player for EmptyArenaSeconds runs the game's own Encounter_Macro_Reset_Arena: it waits until no
fallen player still lies in the arena, removes the boss and every creature of ResetGroups, tells the
arena's volumes Reset, stops the music, clears the fight's sky and goes back to Intro, where zc:reset tells the library and
ResetBehavior has cleared the fight's own flags; the boss rises fresh the next time a player comes
near. Off by default, so a fight without it stands as it was until the library leashes it.
The release runs on the Target sensor alone, so a boss role does not have to send a beacon to
start the fight.
The Target sensor also lets go of a boss that is still alive but has run past TargetRange, and
the defeat beat fires for that too. The library checks the boss at the beat: one still alive, or
gone without dying, was leashed rather than killed, so the run counts as lost, pays nothing and
starts over. The boss is left where it is and the site raises no other while it lives, so keep
TargetRange wide enough to cover the whole arena.
A blocking action list keeps running only while its sensor keeps matching, and a sensor marked
Once is spent after its first tick. So a list that spans ticks (a Timeout, a wait for a spawn)
sits under a plain sensor and ends with the state change that stops it, the way Complete does
here; the content audit warns about a blocking list under a Once sensor.
The rest between fights is the binding row's, not the marker's and not this script's. A manual
spawn marker never reads its own respawn gate (it fires whenever the script asks and its spawn
is dead), and the engine keeps nothing of a script across a chunk load but its id and its
rebound slots, so a Timeout here starts over on every load. So the row's Timing.Rest (an ISO
duration on the world's clock, P1D for one game day) is stamped on this entity at each defeat
and saved with the world, and the ZigRested sensor in the summon leaf below answers false until
the clock is past it. A script that also carries a no-show timeout gates that on ZigRested too,
so a resting site waits quietly in Intro instead of trying its marker. Complete's RearmSeconds
stays the short wait right after a kill; both must pass before the boss rises again.
The eight zc instruction Types, each legal only inside an encounter script: ZigGrant pays the
credited participants a loot reference scaled by share; ZigFeedback draws a FeedbackMoment for
each member; ZigScaleTarget applies the row's health scale to the bound subject now; ZigStunTarget
stuns the subject for a window; ZigControlRule sets the subject's standing crowd-control rule (every
infinite rule effect off, the named one on); ZigMembers is true while the member count is inside a range;
ZigFactor is true while a factor reading about the fight is inside a range; ZigRested is true while
the site carries no rest or the world's clock is past the one its last defeat stamped.
The library reads the zc: beats and nothing else: it credits everyone who fought, scales the
boss's health with the party, pays what the binding row under
Server/ZiggfreedCommon/Encounters names, and fires the feedback moments. Override this file by
id from your own pack to change the skeleton for every script built on it.

SubjectSlot.Description: The target slot the boss is bound into and tracked through. Name the same slot in the binding row's Subject.TargetSlot.

SpawnMarker.Description: The manual-trigger spawn marker that raises the boss. Author one for your boss under Server/NPC/Spawn/Markers and stamp it into the arena.

SummonRange.Description: How far from the encounter entity a spawn marker may be to be fired.

SensorRange.Description: How close a player has to come for the boss to rise, and to count as a member of the fight unless ArenaRange reaches further.

ArenaRange.Description: How far from the encounter entity a player counts as a member of the fight and keeps the arena from an empty reset; SensorRange when smaller, so 0 leaves it SensorRange. Set it to reach the arena's far corners and ledges.

WakeInArena.Description: True: the boss rises only for a player wearing WakeMark, which an ArenaWake volume over the arena puts on whoever stands inside it, so the fight never starts for a player outside the door.

WakeMark.Description: The effect a player inside the arena wears, read when WakeInArena is true.

TargetRange.Description: How far the bound boss may roam before the Target sensor loses it.

BossBarName.Description: The lang key the boss bar shows, resolved on each player's own client.

Music.Description: The MusicContainer started for every member at the release and stopped at the defeat.

FightBehavior.Description: A macro on the Hytale.Instruction.Encounter.Phase.Behavior interface run while the fight is on (its first phase), or $Null for none. Zc_Adds_Wave is one.

Phase2Transition.Description: A macro on the Hytale.Instruction.Encounter.Phase.Transition interface that moves the fight to Phase_2, such as Zc_Phase_At_Health; $Null for a fight with one phase.

Phase2Behavior.Description: A macro on the Phase.Behavior interface run while Phase_2 lasts, or $Null for none.

Phase3Transition.Description: A macro on the Phase.Transition interface that moves the fight from Phase_2 to Phase_3; $Null for none.

Phase3Behavior.Description: A macro on the Phase.Behavior interface run while Phase_3 lasts, or $Null for none.

EveryPhase.Description: A macro on the Phase.Behavior interface run in every phase beside that phase's own behaviour, or $Null for none.

ArenaTag.Description: The tag of the arena's trigger volumes the fight signals: Engaged as it begins, Defeated as the boss falls, Reset as an arena reset ends. Give each arena's volumes the tag its script names.

ArenaSignalRange.Description: How far from the encounter entity a volume carrying ArenaTag hears the fight's signals. Keep it under the distance to the next arena.

ArenaReset.Description: True: a wipe, or an arena with no living player for EmptyArenaSeconds, removes the boss and what ResetGroups names and starts the fight over.

EmptyArenaSeconds.Description: Seconds the arena must hold no living player before an arena reset runs.

ResetGroups.Description: NPC groups an arena reset removes within TargetRange: the boss in every form and what the fight raised.

ResetBehavior.Description: A macro on the Phase.Behavior interface run once as an arena reset begins, to clear the fight's own flags and timers, or $Null for none.

RearmSeconds.Description: How long after the defeat the script waits before it re-arms for the next run, as a [min, max] range.

DefeatReward.Description: The ZigClaim reward (a file under Server/Rewards) paid to every player the win credits, as the fight closes: each finds it under Claims, and in the chest where the boss fell when the binding row stands one. Its own Diminish says how often a player is paid: unwritten, the first win each day on each difficulty. Empty pays none.

Instructions.$Comment: The arena reset, the game's own: it runs whether or not a player is near, so a wipe is seen. Its wipe check runs only while Zc_Encounter_Live is set, which the engage sets only with ArenaReset.

Once per arena reset, whether or not a player is near: the bar comes down, the fight is no longer live, its own flags are cleared, and zc:reset is owed to the library once the boss is gone (Intro sends it).
Back from an arena reset: the library hears zc:reset now the boss is gone.
Every defeat branch comes here. Pays DefeatReward first, while the won run still stands (a leashed or escaped run pays nothing), then waits and re-arms.
